title: If QQQ Repeats Its Last Decade, $100,000 at 40 Could Hit $1 Million by 52
detail:
If QQQ Repeats Its Last Decade, $100,000 at 40 Could Hit $1 Million by 52
Omor Ibne Ehsan
Thu, September 17, 2026 at 1:05 PM MDT 4 min read
QQQ
NVDA
AAPL
MU
AMD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Quick Read

QQQ's 22% trailing-decade pace turns $100,000 into $1 million by 52, but the fund's lifetime 11% rate pushes that milestone to age 63.

QQQ holds zero financial stocks while NVIDIA, Apple, and Micron dominate its top holdings, leaving the fund fully exposed to any mega-cap tech downturn.

A lump-sum investor earns no dollar-cost averaging benefit, making consistent contributions a more controllable retirement lever than chasing an extra point of return.

Read More: Learn 7 secret wealth tips high net worth investors use that most investors miss (sponsor)

A 40-year-old drops $100,000 into QQQ, never adds another dollar, and reaches $1 million by 52. That is the arithmetic if Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) repeats its trailing decade at a roughly 22% annualized NAV return.

DesignRage / Shutterstock.com

QQQ tracks the Nasdaq-100, a nondiversified basket of the 100 largest non-financial companies on the exchange. The same issuer reports a since-inception NAV return of about 11%, which pushes the same $1 million checkpoint to age 63, and an 8% assumption pushes it to 70.

This piece uses QQQ's own numbers to show why a growth investor likely needs a savings rate that does not depend on an exceptional decade repeating itself.

A Scenario Priced Off One Decade

At roughly a 22% annualized NAV return with distributions reinvested, a $100,000 lump sum passes $1 million in about 12 years. For a 40-year-old, that lands at age 52.

Swap in QQQ's roughly 11% since-inception figure and the first full-year checkpoint slides to age 63. Apply a plainer 8%, and the wait stretches to age 70.

QQQ trades near $705, up roughly 501% over the past ten years. That is the run being extrapolated, and it does not repeat by rule.

Why the Next Decade May Not Rhyme

The Nasdaq-100 is concentrated by design. QQQ's largest positions include NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) at about 8%, Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) near 7%, and Micron (NASDAQ:MU) at 6%, with Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), AMD (NASDAQ:AMD), and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) each in the 4% range. Semiconductors carry an unusual share of the fund because the index excludes financials by construction. If AI capex normalizes or memory pricing rolls over, the ETF has no bank or insurer earnings to cushion the drop.

title: Qualcomm Faces Margin Pressure From Rising Costs: Can it Recover?
detail:
Qualcomm Faces Margin Pressure From Rising Costs: Can it Recover?
Zacks Equity Research
Thu, September 17, 2026 at 9:40 AM MDT 4 min read
QCOM
INTC
AMD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Qualcomm Incorporated QCOM is facing near-term margin pressure as rising semiconductor input costs, weaker smartphone demand and an unfavorable product mix weigh on its QCT business. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, QCT EBT margin declined to 26% from 30% a year earlier. The company expects the metric to fall to 23-25% in the fiscal fourth quarter.

The primary pressure is coming from higher costs across the semiconductor supply chain. Qualcomm cited increases in wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, advanced packaging, memory and other materials, which are increasing product costs. QCOM is responding with a price hike. However, it has existing contracts with customers that have fixed prices; hence, it will take several quarters to get margin gains from those price increases.

Qualcomm is also dealing with a weaker mix within the premium handset market. Several handset OEMs are responding to the higher memory costs by changing chip selections and using prior-generation premium processors. This strategy can reduce the average value of the chip mix and put additional pressure on QCT margins.

QCT handset revenues fell 20% year over year to $5.09 billion in the fiscal third quarter as major OEMs reduced purchases. The handset weakness is particularly significant because declines in this business can outweigh growth in Qualcomm's newer markets. The company is seeing a faster reduction in Apple-related revenue. The company now expects its modem share in upcoming iPhone launches to be materially below its earlier 20% assumption. It forecasts Apple product revenue to decline about 50% sequentially from September to December 2026.

Higher operating expenses are adding to the pressure on profitability. The company is investing heavily in data-center products, AI computing and software. This may bring long-term benefits but increases costs in the near term. Management expects the margins to eventually recover once the pricing actions take effect.

How Are Competitors Faring?

Qualcomm faces competition from Intel Corporation INTC and Advanced Micro Devices AMD in the semiconductor space. At the end of the second quarter of 2026, Intel's Non-GAAP operating income was $2.77 billion against an operating loss of $0.5 billion in the year-ago quarter, with respective margins of 17.2% and a negative 3.9%. This is primarily backed by strong demand in several segments and cost discipline initiatives. In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, Client Computing and Physical AI Group revenues rose 15% sequentially to $8.9 billion, with AI PC revenues rising 26% sequentially and representing about two-thirds of segment revenues. In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, Data Center and AI revenues increased 24% sequentially and 59% year over year to $6.3 billion, while operating income rose by $1 billion sequentially to $2.5 billion.

AMD's Operating income jumped 245% to $3.09 billion, while operating margin widened 15 percentage points to 27%. Data Center operating income was $2.1 billion compared with a loss of $155 million in the year-ago quarter, translating into a 31% operating margin. Client and Gaming segment operating income declined 24% year over year to $582 million as higher expenses more than offset the revenue increase. Embedded operating income increased 40% year over year to $386 million. Operating margin improved to 40% from 33%, aided by higher sales and a favorable product mix. Management said embedded x86 products are becoming a meaningful growth driver as hyperscalers and networking customers adopt AMD CPUs for data center control functions.

title: Cerebras Drops 19% in 3 Months: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
detail:
Cerebras Drops 19% in 3 Months: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
Aniruddha Ganguly
Thu, September 17, 2026 at 9:30 AM MDT 5 min read
CBRS
INTC
NVDA
AMD
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Cerebras Systems CBRS shares have dropped 19% in the past three months as profitability, margin pressure, heavy customer concentration, increasing spend on rapid infrastructure expansion and stiff competition continue to spook investors. CBRS' third-quarter 2026 core revenue guidance of $214-$216 million implies only about 2-3% sequential growth from the second quarter of 2026, which failed to impress investors. So, what should they do with the stock? Let's dig deep to find out.

Margin Compression to Hurt CBRS' Near-Term Prospects

Cerebras reported a GAAP net loss of $450.5 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $464.5 million in the first six months of the year. The company had an accumulated deficit of roughly $1.4 billion at the end of the second quarter of 2026 and expects expenses to remain elevated as it invests in research & development, cloud infrastructure and data-center capacity.

In the second quarter of 2026, core gross margin declined 590 basis points (bps) sequentially to 40.6% in the second quarter of 2026 as Cerebras temporarily rented systems back from customers to satisfy strong inference demand. The company expects the third quarter of 2026 to represent the trough, with core gross margin guided to 38-40%, while core operating margin is expected to deteriorate to negative 25-23% from negative 16% in the second quarter of 2026. Although management expects margins to recover as higher-cost rented capacity is replaced by Cerebras-owned systems, the near-term margin pressure likely tempered enthusiasm around the revenue outlook. For 2026, Cerebras now expects core gross margin between 41% and 43%, while operating margin is in the negative 19-17% range.

Cerebras is also perceived as risky by investors due to customer concentration and dependence on OpenAI. Revenues remain concentrated among a small number of customers as three customers individually represented 34%, 32% and 10% of second-quarter 2026 revenues, while a significant portion of Cerebras' $25.4 billion remaining performance obligations (RPO) is tied to its OpenAI agreement. The company acknowledged that OpenAI will remain a meaningful contributor in 2027, even though its share of revenues should decline as AWS and other customers scale.

Cerebras' prospects are suffering from stiff competition from the likes of NVIDIA NVDA, Advanced Micro Devices AMD and Intel INTC in the AI space. NVIDIA is dominating the AI GPU market through its Blackwell, Hopper and DGX/NVL systems that are used for AI training and inference. AMD's MI300 and MI350 accelerator families are competing with CBRS in hyperscale AI infrastructure and enterprise AI clusters. Meanwhile, Intel's Gaudi AI accelerators target enterprise AI training and inference as a lower-cost GPU alternative. Shares of NVIDIA have risen 1.5%, while AMD and Intel dropped 4.6% and 24.6%, respectively.
